meanings.en: to beat, to hit, to strike
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to beat, to hit', paired with 'побить'.

examples.text: Почему меня все бьют в этом доме?
examples.trans: Why does everyone beat me in this house?

examples.text: Тише, Ваня, осторожно! Зачем ты бьёшь дерево ногой?
examples.trans: Easy, Vanya, be careful! Why are you kicking the tree with your foot?

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я знаю всё в моём отеле.
examples.trans: I know everything in my hotel.

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'yesterday' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я вчера ел маринованные грибы. Может, один гриб был плохой.
examples.trans: Yesterday I ate pickled mushrooms. Maybe one mushroom was bad.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Disbelief. Core Russian part meaning 'yes' in everyday speech.
Дай! = give (me)!. Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to give', paired with 'давать'.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: 'два' with masculine/neuter nouns, 'две' with feminine; the noun goes into the genitive singular

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: plural only: there is no singular in everyday use

examples.trans: The money is on the table.
Gum? I didn't have enough money.

meanings.note: Спасибо за + accusative. Core Russian prep meaning 'for; behind' in everyday speech.
+ instrumental. Core Russian prep meaning 'for; behind' in everyday speech.

звонить.gloss: to call, to phone; to ring

meanings.note: + dative of the person. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to call, to phone; to ring', paired with 'позвонить'.
A bell or phone. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to call, to phone; to ring', paired with 'позвонить'.
in the instrumental: 'кем ты работаешь?'

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: мам! = casual 'Mum!' when calling her
+ prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Colloquial. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
hesitation, at the start of a sentence
Ну, папа!. Core Russian part meaning 'well; come on' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'omelette' (originally 'alemelle', thin blade/sheet, describing the flat pan-cooked egg dish).

examples.trans: This is a kind of omelet.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to her', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Она нашла нас на новом месте.
examples.trans: She found us at the new place.
That is it, she got really offended.
She is not answering her phone.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('another, next').

examples.text: Вы квартиры очередников по блату раздавали? Я пятнадцать лет в очереди стою!
examples.trans: Did you hand out waiting-list flats through connections? I've been standing in the queue for fifteen years!

meanings.note: On the phone. Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'звонить'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to call back', paired with 'перезванивать'.

examples.trans: A lucky break: Tretyakov called back.

meanings.note: Informal. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.
As an adverb. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.
Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'казать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to show', paired with 'показывать'.

examples.trans: Shall we show this to Anikeev?

examples.text: Ну, покажите руки. Что у вас за спиной?
examples.trans: Well, show me your hands. What is behind your back?

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'then, later, afterwards' in everyday speech.
'один раз' = once, 'два раза' = twice
Секунду! = One second! / Just a moment!

examples.trans: One second. I'll call right now.
One second. I'll call Mishkin right now.

meanings.note: Смотреть на + accusative. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to look, to watch', paired with 'посмотреть'.
TV, a film. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to look, to watch', paired with 'посмотреть'.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.en: to ask (a question, or someone: спросить у кого-то)
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'просить'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to ask', paired with 'спрашивать'.

examples.text: А спросите у него, куда он дел компьютерный класс.
examples.trans: Ask him where he put the computer lab.

examples.text: Да? А спросите у него, куда он дел компьютерный класс.
examples.trans: Really? Then ask him where he put the computer lab.

meanings.note: As opposed to before. Core Russian adv meaning 'now (from now on)' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Теперь я начальник нашей стройки. Ты уволен!
examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'too, also' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы же здесь выросли. И о людях тоже надо думать.
examples.trans: After all, we grew up here. And you have to think about people too.

meanings.note: the noun after it is genitive plural: тысячи мест

examples.text: Мы построим кластер. Это тысячи рабочих мест.
examples.trans: We will build the cluster. That means thousands of jobs.

meanings.note: Умоляю вас = I'm begging you. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to beg, to implore', paired with 'умолить'.

examples.text: Не бросайте трубку, умоляю вас! Я перед вами стою на коленях.
examples.trans: Don't hang up, I'm begging you! I'm on my knees in front of you.

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'signature' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.

examples.text: Я могу приготовить своё фирменное блюдо.
examples.trans: I can prepare my signature dish.
The chef prepared his signature dish.

meanings.note: + infinitive or a noun. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

Common masculine noun meaning 'wardrobe, cupboard' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The door is behind the wardrobe.

points at something: это моё = that's mine
Linking word: главное — это народ. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.
